text:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate observed for model family 'fast-llama' in us-west-1. current 5xx ~6.8% (>5% threshold). paging eng-oncall.

Alex Chen: i'm on it, pulling traces and the per-model dashboards. looks like the uptick started ~00:45 UTC. correlates with a burst in long-context requests.
Maya Patel: seeing a large RPM spike from a single tenant (acme-corp) on routes /chat/stream and /generate. ~4x normal.
Sergio Gomez: confirmed. KV cache hit ratio dropping and latency tail rising. sounds like token-burst + batching mismatch causing memory pressure.
Alex Chen: quick mitigation options: 1) tenant-scoped throttle, 2) lower TPM for fast-llama family, 3) enable fallback to quantized variant. i prefer (1)+(2) to stop the blast radius fast.
Grace Li: pinging product/AMs about customer impact. @Maya Patel do we know acme-corp plan? Dedicated vs Hosted?
Maya Patel: hosted. we can apply tenant-scoped caps via control-plane. they are not on reserved capacity.
Alex Chen: i'm going to apply a soft throttle to the tenant and drop the family-wide TPM for fast-llama-2 to buy us headroom. will monitor immediately.
Alex Chen: running command now:
```
# apply tenant-scoped soft caps for fast-llama family
rictl rate set --model-family fast-llama --rpm 2000 --tpm 120000 --scope tenant:acme-corp --reason "live mitigation: token burst (auto)"
```
Alex Chen: executed. control-plane acked, changes pushed to routing layer.
incident-bot: ACTION: rate update applied by Alex Chen at 1778009220. new caps: rpm=2000 tpm=120000 for scope tenant:acme-corp on fast-llama family.
Maya Patel: watching metrics — 5xx dropped to ~2.1% within ~90s after the caps. overall latency trending back to baseline.
Sergio Gomez: going to enable fallback for heavy paths to the quantized variant to reduce KV/cache pressure:
```
rictl config set --model fast-llama-2 --fallback-model fast-llama-2-quant --policy immediate --reason "live mitigation: reduce memory/latency"
```
Alex Chen: fallback enabled, no errors surfaced. traffic that exceeds caps started hitting fallback automatically.
Grace Li: document customer impact: acme-corp likely experienced rate-limiting on a subset of high-throughput requests. AM notified and ticket opened. severity P2.
Maya Patel: suggestion: incrementally relax TPM to find stable throughput. propose +10% TPM every 15m while 5xx < 1% and latency stable.
Sergio Gomez: i'll run a single incremental raise in 15m if things stay stable — will post exact commands before doing it.
Oncall Bot: scheduled handoff: Alex Chen -> Grace Li at 1778010200 UTC unless escalated.
Alex Chen: leaving runbook notes in the incident tracker https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-145. initial mitigation: tenant throttle + fallback. flagging follow-ups for SRE/Runtime. grabbing coffee, ping if it regresses :coffee:
Grace Li: taking over monitoring duties. i'll keep an eye for the next 2 hours and coordinate the post-incident retro. please paste any noisy prompts or repros straight into the incident ticket.
Maya Patel: adding a sample noisy prompt from acme-corp to the tracker now.
Sergio Gomez: follow-ups (short list): 1) validate cache eviction metrics and adjust cache sizes if needed, 2) add per-tenant rate alert at 3x baseline to catch this earlier, 3) consider automation: temporary auto-throttle when per-model 5xx > 4% for >60s.
Alex Chen: +1 on automation; that would have reduced manual intervention. great work team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: NOTE: incident summary will be posted to #incidents in ~30m for review and retro prep.
